key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: Unified interpretation of infrared and Raman spectra could help diagnose lattice instabilities in halide perovskites relevant to solar cells.
method: Use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate infrared and Raman spectra.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites.
Connect spectral features to instability symmetry, coupling and dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations across seven materials link slow polar reorientations to very-low-frequency dielectric response and overdamped tilting to persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports spectral simulations, not solar-cell performance gains, and does not quantify agreement with experimental spectra.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
